messages:
dave_oncall: alert ingested: hosted-api p99 spike for model-redwood-open-1, started 12:04 UTC, p99 ~1.8s -> 3.6s, p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s
ben_runtime: looking at runtime metrics now, queue depth on gpu-pool-a spiked, coalescer backlog + KV miss rate climbed
carla_infra: I see a correlated increase in kernel-switch count on those nodes around 12:03, might be kernel-selector churn
alice_sre: any noisy tenant pattern? which tenant IDs show most requests?
ben_runtime: tenant-42 and tenant-echo-ml show a lot of short-seq traffic that would prefer aux-kernel but selector kept switching to primary, causing context rebuilds
perf-bot: profiling snapshot attached: /profiles/5287654321/heap-kernel-dump.json (short sequences, avg seq len 18 tokens, batch variance high)
dave_oncall: past deploy? I see a small heuristic tweak to kselector at 11:58 (reverted on canary?)
carla_infra: it rolled out to prod in two waves; can confirm 11:59 and 12:01. change: "prefer_primary_on_small_batches": true
eve_prod: that change was meant to reduce aux kernel overhead for tiny batches on dedicated hardware — looks like unintended consequences for hosted with noisy small requests
ben_runtime: reproducing locally: when sampler triggers coalesce, a burst of short reqs => selector flips between kernels because recent-sample histogram skews, causing extra priming and KV re-warm costs
ben_runtime: snippet from runtime log: 
```
[12:03:02] selector: candidate=aux kernel_score=0.48 primary_score=0.52 reason=recent_avg_seq_len=20
[12:03:02] priming: evict_kv_cache tenant=tenant-42 size=2.1MB
[12:03:02] coalesce: batch_size=6 variance=4.5 latency_ms=120
```
alice_sre: KV eviction events per second went from ~3/s to ~45/s during spike window, that explains token primes adding ~1s
carla_infra: also see rate limiter behavior — some tenants hit burst windows and got queued behind long-running prime ops, increasing queue depth
dave_oncall: immediate mitigations? suggestions please
ben_runtime: short-term rollback of the kselector heuristic to previous threshold would stop the flipflop; also enable sticky-kernel for 30s per connection to avoid churn
carla_infra: can push a rollback config flag to hosted config within 2 mins, ready to cut
eve_prod: agree rollback + sticky kernel should be safe. we'll monitor cost impact separately
alice_sre: also propose temporary soft-rate-limit per-tenant at burst window to avoid noisy neighbor; can we add a token-bucket cap throttling to tenant-42 for 15m?
carla_infra: can set soft cap 200 RPS for tenant-42 now, yes
ben_runtime: I'll patch selector to prefer current kernel if sequence length delta < 8 tokens (hotfix) and ship a canary right after rollback
dave_oncall: action plan: 1) rollback selector heuristic (carla) 2) enable sticky-kernel 30s (ben) 3) set soft cap tenant-42 15m (carla) 4) monitor p95/p99 and KV eviction rate (alice)
perf-bot: scheduled snapshot collectors for next 15m and alert if p99 > 2s or KV evictions/s > 10
alice_sre: after rollback, p99 dropped to 1.05s within 90s and KV evictions fell to ~6/s, queue depth normalized
ate: thumbs up on rollback, need postmortem to track root cause and guardrails
dave_oncall: assigning owners: ben=runtime fix, carla=infra rollback + soft cap, alice=metrics/dashboard updates, eve=product communication. Please add follow-up doc in #postmortems with timeline and perf graphs
eve_prod: will draft customer note if any impacted tenants ask; ping me if we need to reach out
ben_runtime: follow-up: I'll implement sticky-kernel feature flag and add a unit test for selector hysteresis; will PR and canary by EOD
carla_infra: infra note: we will also add a circuit-breaker to avoid mass eviction when priming rate exceeds threshold
alice_sre: logging todo: instrument kernel-switch count per tenant and export as metric so we can alert on oscillation early
dave_oncall: closing incident thread once postmortem link is up. great triage team :thumbsup:
